clause_text: Either party may terminate this Agreement by giving thirty (30) days prior written notice to the other party.
The employer may terminate the employee immediately without giving any notice period or compensation.
The company may terminate employment at its sole discretion without assigning any reason.
The employer may terminate employment for proven gross misconduct without notice, provided written reasons for termination are given to the employee.
The employee may resign only after serving a notice period of ninety (90) days, while the employer may terminate employment immediately.
Either party may terminate this Agreement for material breach if the breach is not cured within fifteen (15) days after written notice.
The company may terminate this Agreement at any time without notice if it believes the employee's performance is unsatisfactory.
Employment may be terminated after written warning and a reasonable opportunity to improve performance within thirty (30) days.
The employer may dismiss the employee forthwith without enquiry, hearing, or notice for any alleged breach of company policy.
Termination for cause shall require written notice stating the grounds of termination, except where immediate termination is required due to proven fraud or gross misconduct.
The employee shall pay a penalty of Rs. 2 lakhs if employment is terminated before completion of two years.
The employee shall reimburse only actual documented training costs on a proportionate basis if employment is voluntarily terminated within six months of training.
If the employee leaves employment before one year, the employee shall pay liquidated damages equal to twelve months of salary.
If the employee resigns within three months of company-sponsored certification, the company may recover the actual certification fee paid to the training provider.
The company may deduct any amount it considers appropriate from the employee's salary for breach of discipline.
Salary deductions, if any, shall be made only as permitted by applicable law and after written notice to the employee.
The employee shall be liable to compensate the company for all training, recruitment, onboarding, and administrative costs if the employee resigns within two years.
Any training cost recovery shall be limited to reasonable documented expenses directly incurred for specialized external training.
The company may impose penalties on the employee as decided by management from time to time.
Any disciplinary penalty shall be imposed only after written notice, an opportunity to respond, and compliance with applicable employment law.
The employee shall not work for any competing business anywhere in India for three years after leaving employment.
For one year after termination, the employee shall not solicit customers with whom the employee had direct business contact during employment.
The employee shall not engage in any business similar to the company directly or indirectly for five years worldwide.
The employee shall not misuse confidential information or trade secrets after termination of employment.
The employee shall not contact any client of the company after employment for any purpose whatsoever.
The employee shall not solicit company employees to join a competing business for twelve (12) months after termination.
The employee shall not accept employment from any client, vendor, partner, competitor, or associate of the company for three years.
Post-employment restrictions shall apply only to solicitation of active clients and shall not restrict general employment opportunities.
The employee shall not open a similar nature company for three years directly or indirectly after leaving employment.
The employee may work in the same industry after employment provided that the employee does not disclose confidential information or solicit existing clients.
The employee shall maintain confidentiality forever without any exception, limitation, or permitted disclosure.
The employee shall maintain confidentiality for three years after termination, except for information that is public, independently developed, or required to be disclosed by law.
The employee shall not disclose trade secrets for as long as such information remains legally protected as trade secret information.
The employee shall keep all business information confidential during and after employment without any time limit.
Confidential information shall exclude information that becomes public through no fault of the employee or is required to be disclosed by law.
The employee shall be liable for any disclosure of company information whether intentional, accidental, direct, or indirect, without limitation.
Each party shall protect confidential information using reasonable care and shall notify the other party of unauthorized disclosure.
The receiving party shall not disclose confidential information except to employees or advisors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality duties.
The employee shall not use any information learned during employment for any purpose after termination, even if such information is generally known.
Confidentiality obligations shall not prevent the employee from using general skills, experience, and knowledge acquired during employment.
All ideas, inventions, works, or intellectual property created by the employee at any time shall be the exclusive property of the company.
All intellectual property created by the employee during employment using company resources or relating to company business shall belong to the company.
The employee retains ownership of intellectual property created before employment or outside employment without using company resources.
The employee irrevocably assigns all present and future intellectual property rights to the company without additional consideration.
The company shall own source code developed by the employee as part of assigned employment duties.
The company may claim ownership over all software, hardware, designs, ideas, notes, and concepts developed by the employee whether or not related to company business.
Employee inventions created independently outside working hours without using company confidential information shall remain the employee's property.
The employee shall execute reasonable documents required to confirm company ownership of employment-related intellectual property.
The employee waives all moral rights and author rights in all works created before, during, and after employment.
The employee grants the company a limited license to use employee-owned background materials only as necessary for company business.
The employer may modify the employment agreement or company policies from time to time and such changes shall apply immediately.
Any amendment to this Agreement shall be valid only if made in writing and signed by both parties.
The company guidelines may be updated after reasonable notice to employees, provided such changes do not reduce existing contractual rights without consent.
The employer may change salary structure, work location, job role, and benefits at any time without employee consent.
Changes to job duties may be made based on business needs after reasonable notice to the employee.
Company rules shall be binding on employees immediately upon publication, whether or not communicated individually.
Company policies shall be communicated to employees by email or internal portal before becoming applicable.
The employer reserves full rights to alter employment terms as and when required.
Material changes to employment terms shall require prior written consent of both employer and employee.
The employee shall comply with company policies as updated from time to time, provided such policies are lawful and communicated in writing.
issue: Policy updates from time to time

clause_text: The employee shall be liable for all losses, damages, costs, and expenses suffered by the company without any limitation.
The employee shall be responsible only for direct losses caused by proven misconduct or breach, subject to applicable law.
The company shall not be liable under any circumstances for any loss suffered by the employee.
Neither party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages except in cases of fraud or wilful misconduct.
The employee shall compensate the company for any grave or remote loss as calculated by management.
Liability for employee misconduct shall be limited to actual direct loss proven through due process.
The employee shall be personally liable for all claims made by clients against the company arising during employment.
The company may recover losses from the employee only after establishing negligence, fraud, or wilful misconduct through proper process.
The employee shall bear losses caused by system failure, customer complaint, or business loss whether or not caused by the employee.
Each party shall remain responsible for losses caused by its own negligence, fraud, or wilful misconduct.
Each party shall indemnify the other for losses arising from its own breach, negligence, fraud, or wilful misconduct, subject to reasonable limits.
The employee shall indemnify and keep indemnified the company against all claims, losses, damages, and expenses without any limit.
The company shall indemnify the employee for claims arising from lawful actions taken within the scope of employment.
The employee shall defend the company against all third-party claims regardless of whether the employee caused the claim.
Indemnity obligations shall apply only to claims arising from breach, negligence, fraud, or wilful misconduct of the indemnifying party.
The employee shall indemnify the company for any loss, whether direct or indirect, actual or remote, arising from employment.
Each party shall promptly notify the other of any claim for which indemnity is sought.
The indemnifying party shall not settle any claim without the prior written consent of the indemnified party, not to be unreasonably withheld.
The employee's indemnity obligation shall survive forever and apply to all claims of any nature without limitation.
Indemnity obligations shall survive termination only for claims arising during the term of employment and subject to applicable limitation periods.
Neither party shall be liable for delay or failure caused by events beyond reasonable control, provided prompt notice is given.
The company may terminate the agreement due to force majeure without refund, compensation, or liability.
Force majeure events shall include natural disasters, war, government restrictions, strikes, pandemics, and events beyond reasonable control.
Only the company may invoke force majeure, and the employee shall have no claim arising from such event.
The affected party shall notify the other party within seven (7) days of a force majeure event and use reasonable efforts to mitigate its impact.
If force majeure continues for more than ninety (90) days, either party may terminate the agreement without penalty.
The company shall not be required to provide notice or compensation during any force majeure event.
Payment obligations already accrued before a force majeure event shall remain payable unless prohibited by law.
The employer may suspend all employee rights during force majeure at its sole discretion.
issue: Suspension of rights at sole discretion

clause_text: Force majeure shall not excuse obligations relating to confidentiality, data protection, or payment already due.
Salary shall be paid monthly on or before the seventh day of the following month.
The company may withhold salary if the employee fails to meet objectives or targets decided by the company.
Performance incentives may be withheld if documented and agreed performance targets are not achieved.
The employer may revise salary and benefits at any time based on management decision.
Salary revisions shall be communicated in writing and shall not reduce fixed salary without employee consent unless permitted by law.
The employee shall not be entitled to salary during the notice period if the employee resigns.
The employee shall receive salary for all days actually worked, including any applicable notice period served.
Bonus payments are discretionary and may be paid based on company policy and individual performance.
The employee shall reimburse the company for all overpaid amounts after receiving written explanation of the overpayment.
The company may deduct any amount from salary for any alleged loss without notice.
Any dispute arising under this Agreement shall first be resolved through good faith discussion and then referred to arbitration.
All disputes shall be decided finally by the company's board and such decision shall be binding on the employee.
The sole arbitrator shall be appointed only by the company and the employee shall have no objection to such appointment.
The arbitrator shall be appointed mutually by both parties in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
The employee waives the right to approach any court or authority for any employment-related claim.
Nothing in this clause shall prevent either party from seeking interim relief from a court of competent jurisdiction.
The decision of management regarding any dispute shall be final and binding on the employee.
Administrative disputes may be escalated to a neutral committee with representatives of both parties.
All disputes shall be resolved only in a distant jurisdiction selected by the company.
This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of India and courts at the mutually agreed jurisdiction shall have authority.
The employee agrees to biometric monitoring and continuous workplace surveillance at all times during employment.
Employee personal data shall be collected only for legitimate employment purposes and processed according to applicable data protection laws.
The company may monitor all employee communications, devices, location, and personal accounts without notice.
The company may monitor company-owned systems for security and compliance after providing notice to employees.
The employee consents to collection and processing of sensitive personal data for any business purpose determined by the company.
Sensitive personal data shall be processed only with consent, legal basis, security safeguards, and purpose limitation.
The employer may share employee personal data with affiliates, vendors, or third parties without notice.
Employee data may be shared with service providers only for employment-related purposes subject to confidentiality and security obligations.
The company shall retain employee data only for as long as required by law or legitimate business purpose.
The company may retain employee personal data permanently for future business purposes.
